title.en: A Journey to the Magical Mountains
Minam and her grandfather in the Himalayas

text.en: Minam, a young girl at the foot of the Himalayas, goes on a special walk with her grandfather, who was once a Sherpa. They picnic by a river, meet yaks, build a snowman, see Mount Everest and promise to protect the mountains. In this chapter you will read the story, learn mountain words, use body-part names for objects, and join sentences with and, or, but and because.

Minam lived in a small village at the foot of the mighty Himalayas. She loved listening to her grandfather's stories about the mountains, because he was once a Sherpa. One sunny morning her grandfather said that she had become strong enough to walk a long distance, so he would take her on a special journey to see the Himalayas up close. Minam was excited and packed rotis with pickle, two water bottles and her favourite fruit, apples.
They set out early in the morning. On the way Minam saw beautiful flowers and tall trees and heard bird sounds she had never heard before. The air was fresh and cool, and Minam felt very happy. At a small river with clear water, her grandfather said this is where they would have lunch. They enjoyed their rotis by the river, watched the fish swim, and Minam dipped her feet in the cool water and laughed while eating an apple.
After lunch they climbed higher, and soon they saw yaks. Her grandfather said yaks are very important to mountain people, as they give milk and wool and carry heavy loads. Higher up the ground was covered with snow, which Minam had never seen so much of before. She and her grandfather made a small snowman, laughed and played, and made memories that she would value forever.
Finally they reached the top of a hill and Minam saw the huge peaks of the Himalayas shining in the sun. Her grandfather pointed to the highest mountain and said that it was Mount Everest, the tallest mountain in the world, which many brave people have tried to climb. Minam felt happy to be living near such wonderful mountains.
As the sun set they started back. On the way they heard beautiful music played by an old man under a tree. They saw a family of mountain goats jumping from rock to rock, and her grandfather explained that goats are good at climbing and can reach places that are hard for people. They reached the village when it was dark. Minam was tired but very happy and thanked her grandfather, saying she would never forget the day. He replied that the mountains are truly magical, because they teach us strength, beauty and the wonders of nature, and that we must respect and protect them. Minam promised to take care of the mountains and share their magic with everyone she met.
The Himalayas are the tallest mountain range in the world. A Sherpa is a guide who helps climbers in the mountains. A summit is the top of a mountain, a slope is the side that goes up or down, and the foot is the bottom of the mountain. A valley is a low area of land between mountains and a plateau is a high flat land. A plain is a wide flat area, and a mountain range is a long row of mountains. A journey is a trip from one place to another. Memories are things we remember and cherish. Yaks are large strong animals used for milk, wool and carrying loads.
We use names of body parts for things: legs of a table, hands of a clock, foot of a mountain and neck of a bottle. Mouth of a river, arm of a chair, heart of a city, ear of corn and eye of a needle are more examples. This is called figurative use, because the object is compared to a body part.
Words that join words, phrases or sentences are called conjunctions. And adds information: I have a dog and a cat. Or gives a choice: Do you want an apple or a banana? But shows a difference: I was tired, but I finished my homework. Because gives a reason: I stayed inside because it was raining. She was hungry, so she ate a sandwich could also be written as She ate a sandwich because she was hungry. Choose the conjunction by asking whether you are adding, choosing, contrasting or giving a reason.

problem.en: Join with the right conjunction: He ran fast. He missed the bus.

text.en: The second fact is surprising after the first.
Use but.
So: He ran fast but he missed the bus.

why.en: And would not show the difference.

problem.en: What is the foot of a mountain?

text.en: Think about the body part foot.
The foot of a mountain is the bottom, where the mountain meets the land.

why.en: It is not a real foot.

text.en: So the foot of the mountain is its lowest part.

prompt.en: Tell the story of Minam's journey and what she promised her grandfather.

requiredIdeas.en: A long walk with her grandfather
River picnic, yaks, snow and Mount Everest

points.en: Minam and her grandfather went on a journey to the Himalayas.
They saw yaks, snow, Mount Everest and mountain goats.
Mountains teach us strength and beauty and must be protected.
The foot of a mountain is its bottom; the summit is its top.
And, or, but and because join sentences in different ways.
